content.text:
**Investigation summary:** Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "books", and "monitor" return no vendor audit or usage-verification right. The two candidate sections confirm this:

- **§ 5/6 Compensation (p0045, p0047):** fee mechanics run one way — TrueLink invoices and *Client* is entitled to supporting documentation and to contest charges. No vendor right to examine Client's books or usage.
- **§ 8 Covenants of Client (p0051–p0058):** compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only, with no inspection or reporting-on-demand right. § 8(f) (p0058) lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms on *its own* Interface to block spamming — a self-help control over vendor infrastructure, not an audit of, or access to, Client systems.
- **§ 3(e) (p0037):** transparency runs in our favour — Client gets real-time usage statistics and raw log files.
- **§ 9 (p0060):** the only access obligation is Client providing reasonable access so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at its own cost — a vendor remediation duty benefiting us, not a verification right.

The absence of any audit right leaves us better off than the preferred position, so there is nothing to limit and no redline is warranted; proposing audit machinery would only create an obligation against us.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
input.rationale: The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right over Client's usage, records or systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "books" and "monitor" return nothing, and the two candidate locations contain no such right: § 5/6 (p0045, p0047) is a one-way transparency provision under which Client receives documentation supporting charges and may contest them, and § 8 Covenants of Client (p0051-p0058) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties. § 8(f) (p0058) permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms on its own Interface to prevent spamming, which is self-help over vendor infrastructure rather than an audit of or remote access to Client systems. Related provisions run in our favour: § 3(e) (p0037) gives Client real-time access to usage statistics and raw log files, and § 9 (p0060) requires only that Client provide reasonable access so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at TrueLink's sole cost. With no audit right binding the Customer, our position is better than the preferred one (no frequency, notice, cost or system-access limits are needed because there is nothing to limit), and this is not treated as a "missing" clause since the rule is protective and inserting audit machinery would create an obligation against us. Worth noting for context only, and not a deviation: because there is no express audit clause, if TrueLink later requests usage verification there are no contractual guardrails, so we should resist any vendor attempt to add audit rights without the preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access).
